question: The sale bill of an article after two successive discounts of 20% each is ₹16,000. The MRP of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount = a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100 ⇒ 20 + 20 − (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 36%.

Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 36% = 64%.

Given 64% = ₹16,000.

MRP (100%) = (16,000 ÷ 64) × 100 = 250 × 100 = ₹25,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP = ₹16,000, First Discount (d₁) = 20%, Second Discount (d₂) = 20%.

**Formula:** SP = MRP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5580759df8fe034d63f9d29f4b1ee3325efb2e38b30ab7b811f535d2ecfccd3.png] 

⇒ 16,000 = MRP × (80 ÷ 100) × (80 ÷ 100)

⇒ 16,000 = MRP × (4 ÷ 5) × (4 ÷ 5)

⇒ 16,000 = MRP × (16 ÷ 25)

⇒ MRP = (16,000 × 25) ÷ 16

⇒ MRP = 1,000 × 25 = ₹25,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another, the net discount is calculated on the reducing balance or by using the formula x + y − xy/100.

Marked Price (MRP)

It is the price printed on an article. Discounts are always calculated on the **Marked Price** to reach the **Selling Price**.
